topic: Vertex of a quadratic: projectile maximum height
problem: A ball is thrown upward from the top of a platform. The height of the ball above the ground, in feet, t seconds after it is thrown is given by h(t) = -16t^2 + 72t + 5. What is the maximum height, in feet, that the ball reaches?

bad.why: Rewriting -16t^2+72t+5 in vertex form by hand involves factoring out -16 and fractions; clicking the vertex gives (2.25, 86) directly.
Invalid here: the quadratic formula finds when the ball hits the ground (h=0), not its maximum height.

algebraFirst.description: Recalls the vertex formula t=-b/(2a)=72/32=2.25, then substitutes back to compute h(2.25)=-81+162+5=86.

explanationNotes: The maximum height is the highest point of the parabola, its vertex, (2.25, 86). Make clear that the x-coordinate is the time (2.25 seconds) and the y-coordinate is the height, so the answer is 86, not 2.25.
